verses.1:1: The book of the lineage of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
verses.1:2: Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,
verses.1:3: and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram,
verses.1:4: and Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.1:5: and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,
verses.1:6: and Jesse fathered David the king. And David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah,
verses.1:7: and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph,
verses.1:8: and Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah,
verses.1:9: and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,
verses.1:10: and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,
verses.1:11: and Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
verses.1:12: And after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,
verses.1:13: and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,
verses.1:14: and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,
verses.1:15: and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob,
verses.1:16: and Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.
verses.1:17: Therefore all the generations from Abraham until David are fourteen generations, and from David until the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon until the Christ, fourteen generations.
verses.1:18: Now the birth of Jesus Christ came about in this way: after His mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:19: Now Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wanting to expose her publicly, decided to divorce her secretly.
verses.1:20: But after he had pondered these things, look, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:21: And she will give birth to a son, and you will call His name Jesus, for He Himself will save His people from their sins."
verses.1:22: Now all of this has happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying,
verses.1:23: "Look, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call His name Immanuel," which translated means, "God with us."
verses.1:24: And when Joseph woke from sleep, he did just as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife,
verses.1:25: and he did not know her until she gave birth to a son; and he called His name Jesus.
verses.2:1: Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, look, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
verses.2:2: saying, "Where is He who was born king of the Jews? For we saw His star in the east, and we came to worship Him."
verses.2:3: And when King Herod heard it, he was disturbed, and all of Jerusalem with him.
verses.2:4: And having assembled all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he was inquiring from them where the Christ was to be born.
verses.2:5: And they said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, for so it has been written through the prophet:
verses.2:6: 'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the rulers of Judah; for from you a ruler will come out who will shepherd My people Israel.'"
verses.2:7: Then Herod, secretly summoning the magi, ascertained precisely from them the time of the star's appearance.
verses.2:8: And sending them to Bethlehem, he said, "Go and search carefully concerning the child; and as soon as you find Him, report back to me, so that I too may come and worship Him."
verses.2:9: And after listening to the king, they went on their way; and look, the star that they had seen in the east was going ahead of them, until it came and stood over where the child was.
verses.2:10: And on seeing the star, they rejoiced with an exceedingly great joy.
verses.2:11: And coming into the house, they saw the child with Mary His mother; and falling down, they worshiped Him. And opening their treasures, they offered Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
verses.2:12: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their own country by another route.
verses.2:13: Now after they had withdrawn, look, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Rise, take the child and His mother, flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod is about to seek the child in order to destroy Him."
verses.2:14: So he rose, took the child and His mother by night, and withdrew into Egypt,
verses.2:15: and he was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying, "Out of Egypt I called My Son."
verses.2:16: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, became exceedingly angry, and he sent and put to death all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its surrounding districts, two years old and under, according to the time that he had ascertained precisely from the magi.
verses.2:17: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
verses.2:18: "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and much lamentation; Rachel weeping for her children, and she was unwilling to be comforted, because they are no more."
verses.2:19: Now when Herod died, look, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
verses.2:20: saying, "Rise, take the child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child's life have died."
verses.2:21: So he rose, took the child and His mother, and entered the land of Israel.
verses.2:22: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and having been warned in a dream, he withdrew into the districts of Galilee,
verses.2:23: and arriving there, he settled in a city called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets would be fulfilled, that He will be called a Nazarene.
verses.3:1: Now in those days John the Baptist arrived, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
verses.3:2: saying, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near."
verses.3:3: For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, "The voice of one calling out in the wilderness: 'Make ready the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.'"
verses.3:4: Now John himself had clothing made from camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
verses.3:5: Then Jerusalem was going out to him, and all Judea and all the surrounding region of the Jordan,
verses.3:6: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River as they confessed their sins.
verses.3:7: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
verses.3:8: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance,
verses.3:9: and do not presume to say within yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father,' for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
verses.3:10: Already indeed the ax lies at the root of the trees; every tree, therefore, that does not produce good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.
verses.3:11: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, yet He who comes after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; He Himself will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.3:12: His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will clean out His threshing floor thoroughly and gather His wheat into the granary, while He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."
verses.3:13: Then Jesus arrived from Galilee at the Jordan to John in order to be baptized by him.
verses.3:14: But John was trying to hinder Him, saying, "I have need to be baptized by You, and You are coming to me?"
verses.3:15: But answering, Jesus said to him, "Allow it for now, for in this way it is proper for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he allowed Him.
verses.3:16: And having been baptized, Jesus immediately came up out of the water; and look, the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, coming upon Him.
verses.3:17: And look, a voice came from the heavens, saying, "This is My Son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased."
verses.4:1: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
verses.4:2: And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward He became hungry.
verses.4:3: And the tempter approached and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves of bread."
verses.4:4: But answering, He said, "It is written, 'Not on bread alone will a person live, but on every word going forth through the mouth of God.'"
verses.4:5: Then the devil took Him along into the holy city and placed Him on the pinnacle of the temple,
verses.4:6: and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down, for it is written, 'To His angels He will give orders concerning You, and on their hands they will lift You up, so that You never strike Your foot against a stone.'"
verses.4:7: Jesus said to him, "Again, it is written, 'You shall not test the Lord your God.'"
verses.4:8: Again, the devil took Him along to an exceedingly high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
verses.4:9: and said to Him, "I will give all these things to You if You fall down and worship me."
verses.4:10: Then Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan! For it is written, 'The Lord your God you shall worship, and Him alone you shall serve.'"
verses.4:11: Then the devil left Him, and look, angels approached and were serving Him.
verses.4:12: Now when He heard that John had been handed over, He withdrew into Galilee.
verses.4:13: And leaving Nazareth, He came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the district of Zebulun and Naphtali,
verses.4:14: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
verses.4:15: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations—
verses.4:16: the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in the region and shadow of death, a light dawned on them."
verses.4:17: From that time Jesus began to proclaim and to say, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near."
verses.4:18: Now while walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, throwing a casting net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.4:19: And He said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you fishers of people."
verses.4:20: And immediately leaving the nets, they followed Him.
verses.4:21: And going farther from there, He saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, repairing their nets, and He called them.
verses.4:22: And immediately leaving the boat and their father, they followed Him.
verses.4:23: And He was going around throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every ailment among the people.
verses.4:24: And the report about Him went out into all Syria, and they brought to Him all who were unwell, those gripped by various diseases and severe pains, the demon-possessed and epileptics and paralytics, and He healed them.
verses.4:25: And great crowds followed Him from Galilee and the Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.
verses.5:1: Now upon seeing the crowds, He went up onto the mountain; and after He sat down, His disciples came up to Him.
verses.5:2: And opening His mouth, He began teaching them, saying,
verses.5:3: "Blessed are those who are poor in spirit, because the kingdom of the heavens belongs to them.
verses.5:4: Blessed are those who grieve, because they themselves will be comforted.
verses.5:5: Blessed are the gentle, because they themselves will inherit the earth.
verses.5:6: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, because they themselves will be satisfied.
verses.5:7: Blessed are the merciful, because they themselves will be shown mercy.
verses.5:8: Blessed are those who are pure in heart, because they themselves will see God.
verses.5:9: Blessed are the peacemakers, because they themselves will be called sons of God.
verses.5:10: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness, because the kingdom of the heavens belongs to them.
verses.5:11: Blessed are you whenever people insult you and persecute you and falsely speak every kind of evil against you on My account.
verses.5:12: Rejoice and be overjoyed, because your reward is great in the heavens; for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who came before you.
verses.5:13: You yourselves are the salt of the earth; yet if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown outside and trampled underfoot by people.
verses.5:14: You yourselves are the light of the world. A city situated on top of a mountain cannot be hidden;
verses.5:15: neither do people light a lamp and place it beneath a measuring basket, but rather on the lampstand, and it shines for everyone who is in the house.
verses.5:16: In the same way, let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good deeds and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.
verses.5:17: Do not suppose that I came to annul the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to annul, but to fulfill.
verses.5:18: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single iota nor a single stroke of a letter will ever pass away from the Law until everything comes to pass.
verses.5:19: Therefore, whoever sets aside one of the least of these commandments and teaches people accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; yet whoever practices and teaches them, this person will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
verses.5:20: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
verses.5:21: You have heard that it was told to those of ancient times, 'You must not murder, and whoever murders will be liable to judgment.'
verses.5:22: Yet I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, 'Raca,' will be liable to the Sanhedrin; and whoever says, 'You fool,' will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
verses.5:23: So if you are presenting your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
verses.5:24: leave your gift there in front of the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come back and present your gift.
verses.5:25: Come to friendly terms with your legal opponent quickly while you are on the road with him, so that the opponent does not hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you get thrown into prison.
verses.5:26: Truly I tell you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid back the very last quadrans.
verses.5:27: You have heard that it was said, 'You must not commit adultery.'
verses.5:28: Yet I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
verses.5:29: Now if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your body parts be lost than for your entire body to be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.5:30: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your body parts be lost than for your entire body to go off into Gehenna.
verses.5:31: Furthermore, it was said, 'Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.'
verses.5:32: Yet I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, causes her to become an adulteress, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
verses.5:33: Again, you have heard that it was told to those of ancient times, 'You must not swear falsely, but you must fulfill your oaths to the Lord.'
verses.5:34: Yet I tell you not to swear an oath at all: neither by heaven, because it is God's throne;
verses.5:35: nor by the earth, because it is the footstool for His feet; nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the Great King;
verses.5:36: nor should you swear by your head, because you cannot make a single hair white or black.
verses.5:37: Instead, let your statement be 'Yes, yes,' or 'No, no'; anything beyond these comes from the evil one.
verses.5:38: You have heard that it was said, 'Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.'
verses.5:39: Yet I tell you not to resist an evil person; rather, whoever slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other one to him as well;
verses.5:40: and to the one who wants to take you to court and obtain your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
verses.5:41: and whoever compels you into service for one mile, go along with him for two.
verses.5:42: Give to the one who asks from you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
verses.5:43: You have heard that it was said, 'You must love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
verses.5:44: Yet I tell you: love your enemies and pray on behalf of those who persecute you,
verses.5:45: so that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; because He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.5:46: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the very same thing?
verses.5:47: And if you greet only your brothers, what extraordinary thing are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the very same thing?
verses.5:48: Therefore, you yourselves must be complete, just as your heavenly Father is complete."
verses.6:1: "Now take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father who is in the heavens.
verses.6:2: Therefore, when you do an act of charity, do not sound a trumpet before you, just as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be honored by people. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:3: But when you do an act of charity, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
verses.6:4: so that your act of charity may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:5: And when you pray, you must not be like the hypocrites; for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the corners of the wide streets, so that they may be seen by people. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:6: But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:7: And when you pray, do not babble repetitively just as the Gentiles do, for they suppose that they will be heard because of their many words.
verses.6:8: Therefore, do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
verses.6:9: You, then, pray in this way: 'Our Father who is in the heavens, may Your name be held holy,
verses.6:10: may Your kingdom come, may Your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
verses.6:11: Give us today our daily bread;
verses.6:12: and forgive us our debts, just as we also have forgiven our debtors.
verses.6:13: And do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.'
verses.6:14: For if you forgive people their transgressions, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
verses.6:15: But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your transgressions.
verses.6:16: Now when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may be seen by people to be fasting. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.6:17: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
verses.6:18: so that you may not be seen by people to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
verses.6:19: Do not store up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and corrosion ruin them, and where thieves break in and steal;
verses.6:20: but store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor corrosion ruins them, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
verses.6:21: For where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
verses.6:22: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore, if your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light;
verses.6:23: but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If, therefore, the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
verses.6:24: No one is able to serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
verses.6:25: For this reason I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
verses.6:26: Look closely at the birds of the sky: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they are?
verses.6:27: And which of you by being anxious is able to add a single cubit to his lifespan?
verses.6:28: And why are you anxious about clothing? Observe closely how the lilies of the field grow: they neither toil nor spin;
verses.6:29: yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
verses.6:30: Now if God clothes the grass of the field in this way, which exists today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, will He not much more clothe you, you of little faith?
verses.6:31: Therefore, do not be anxious, saying, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we wear?'
verses.6:32: For the Gentiles eagerly seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all of them.
verses.6:33: But seek first the kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
verses.6:34: Therefore, do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Enough for the day is its own trouble."
verses.7:1: "Do not judge, so that you will not be judged;
verses.7:2: for with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged, and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
verses.7:3: And why do you look at the splinter that is in your brother's eye, yet do not notice the beam in your own eye?
verses.7:4: Or how will you say to your brother, 'Let me take the splinter out of your eye,' when look, the beam is in your own eye?
verses.7:5: Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the splinter out of your brother's eye.
verses.7:6: Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, so that they do not trample them under their feet and turn and tear you to pieces.
verses.7:7: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened for you.
verses.7:8: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
verses.7:9: Or what person is there among you whose son will ask him for bread—will he hand him a stone?
verses.7:10: Or if he also asks for a fish—will he hand him a snake?
verses.7:11: If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask Him!
verses.7:12: Therefore, everything that you want people to do for you, do in the same way for them also; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.7:13: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it.
verses.7:14: For narrow is the gate and constricted is the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
verses.7:15: Watch out for false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, yet inwardly are ravenous wolves.
verses.7:16: By their fruits you will recognize them. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
verses.7:17: In this way, every good tree produces fine fruit, but the diseased tree produces bad fruit.
verses.7:18: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a diseased tree produce fine fruit.
verses.7:19: Every tree that does not produce fine fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.7:20: So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.
verses.7:21: Not everyone who says to Me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of My Father who is in the heavens.
verses.7:22: Many will say to Me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons, and in Your name perform many mighty works?'
verses.7:23: And then I will declare to them, 'I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness.'
verses.7:24: Therefore, everyone who hears these words of Mine and does them will be likened to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
verses.7:25: And the rain came down, and the torrents came, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, for it had been founded on the rock.
verses.7:26: And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not do them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
verses.7:27: And the rain came down, and the torrents came, and the winds blew and struck against that house; and it fell, and its collapse was great."
verses.7:28: And it happened when Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astonished at His teaching;
verses.7:29: for He was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
verses.8:1: Now when He had come down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.
verses.8:2: And look, a leper approached and bowed down before Him, saying, "Lord, if You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.8:3: And stretching out His hand, He touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
verses.8:4: And Jesus said to him, "See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them."
verses.8:5: Now when He entered Capernaum, a centurion approached Him, appealing to Him,
verses.8:6: and saying, "Lord, my servant is lying paralyzed in the house, severely tormented."
verses.8:7: And He said to him, "I will come and heal him."
verses.8:8: But the centurion answered and said, "Lord, I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof; but only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.
verses.8:9: For I too am a man set under authority, having soldiers under myself; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
verses.8:10: Now when Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those who were following, "Truly I say to you, with no one in Israel have I found such great faith.
verses.8:11: And I say to you that many will come from east and west and will recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
verses.8:12: but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.8:13: And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; just as you have believed, let it be done for you." And the servant was healed in that hour.
verses.8:14: And when Jesus came into Peter's house, He saw his mother-in-law lying down and sick with a fever.
verses.8:15: And He touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she got up and began serving Him.
verses.8:16: Now when evening came, they brought to Him many who were demon-possessed; and He cast out the spirits with a word, and He healed all who were ill,
verses.8:17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "He Himself took our weaknesses and bore our diseases."
verses.8:18: Now when Jesus saw a crowd around Him, He gave orders to depart to the other side.
verses.8:19: And a scribe approached and said to Him, "Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go."
verses.8:20: And Jesus said to him, "The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head."
verses.8:21: And another of the disciples said to Him, "Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father."
verses.8:22: But Jesus said to him, "Follow Me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
verses.8:23: And when He got into a boat, His disciples followed Him.
verses.8:24: And look, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; yet He Himself was sleeping.
verses.8:25: And they came and woke Him, saying, "Lord, save us; we are perishing!"
verses.8:26: And He said to them, "Why are you timid, you of little faith?" Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
verses.8:27: And the men marveled, saying, "What sort of person is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him?"
verses.8:28: And when He came to the other side, into the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men coming out of the tombs met Him, so extremely fierce that no one was able to pass along that road.
verses.8:29: And look, they cried out, saying, "What do we have to do with You, Son of God? Have You come here to torment us before the time?"
verses.8:30: Now at a distance from them there was a herd of many pigs feeding.
verses.8:31: And the demons were imploring Him, saying, "If You cast us out, send us away into the herd of pigs."
verses.8:32: And He said to them, "Go." So they came out and went into the pigs; and look, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
verses.8:33: And the herdsmen fled, and going away into the city, they reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
verses.8:34: And look, the whole city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw Him, they implored Him to depart from their borders.
verses.9:1: And getting into a boat, He crossed over and came to His own city.
verses.9:2: And look, they were bringing to Him a paralyzed man lying on a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralyzed man, "Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven."
verses.9:3: And look, some of the scribes said within themselves, "This man is blaspheming."
verses.9:4: And Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said, "Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
verses.9:5: For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
verses.9:6: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—then He said to the paralyzed man, "Get up, pick up your bed, and go to your house."
verses.9:7: And he got up and went away to his house.
verses.9:8: And when the crowds saw this, they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
verses.9:9: And as Jesus was passing on from there, He saw a man sitting at the tax booth, called Matthew, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And he rose and followed Him.
verses.9:10: And it happened that as He was reclining at table in the house, look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and His disciples.
verses.9:11: And when the Pharisees saw this, they were saying to His disciples, "Why does your Teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.9:12: But when He heard this, He said, "Those who are healthy do not have need of a physician, but those who are ill.
verses.9:13: Now go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.9:14: Then the disciples of John came to Him, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast, while Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.9:15: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? Yet the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
verses.9:16: And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for its patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear occurs.
verses.9:17: Nor do people put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wineskins burst, and the wine pours out and the wineskins are ruined. Instead, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."
verses.9:18: While He was speaking these things to them, look, a ruler approached and bowed down before Him, saying, "My daughter has just died; yet come and lay Your hand on her, and she will live."
verses.9:19: And Jesus got up and followed him, as did His disciples.
verses.9:20: And look, a woman who had been suffering from a flow of blood for twelve years approached from behind and touched the fringe of His garment,
verses.9:21: for she kept saying within herself, "If I only touch His garment, I will be made well."
verses.9:22: But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, "Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well." And the woman was made well from that hour.
verses.9:23: And when Jesus came into the house of the ruler and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,
verses.9:24: He said, "Leave, for the girl has not died, but is sleeping." And they were laughing at Him.
verses.9:25: But when the crowd had been put outside, He entered and took hold of her hand, and the girl got up.
verses.9:26: And this report went out into all that land.
verses.9:27: And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out and saying, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.9:28: And when He entered the house, the blind men approached Him, and Jesus said to them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They said to Him, "Yes, Lord."
verses.9:29: Then He touched their eyes, saying, "According to your faith let it be done for you."
verses.9:30: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them, saying, "See that no one knows about it."
verses.9:31: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout all that land.
verses.9:32: Now as they were going out, look, they brought to Him a mute man who was demon-possessed.
verses.9:33: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke; and the crowds marveled, saying, "Never has anything like this been seen in Israel."
verses.9:34: But the Pharisees were saying, "By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons."
verses.9:35: And Jesus was going around through all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness.
verses.9:36: And seeing the crowds, He felt compassion for them, because they were troubled and cast down, like sheep having no shepherd.
verses.9:37: Then He said to His disciples, "The harvest indeed is plentiful, yet the workers are few.
verses.9:38: Therefore plead with the Lord of the harvest that He may send out workers into His harvest."
verses.10:1: And calling His twelve disciples to Himself, He gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every affliction.
verses.10:2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; and James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
verses.10:3: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
verses.10:4: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the one who also betrayed Him.
verses.10:5: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them and saying, "Do not go onto a road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans;
verses.10:6: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
verses.10:7: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
verses.10:8: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Without cost you received; without cost give.
verses.10:9: Do not acquire gold, nor silver, nor copper for your belts,
verses.10:10: no bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.
verses.10:11: And into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and remain there until you leave.
verses.10:12: And as you enter the house, greet it.
verses.10:13: And if indeed the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
verses.10:14: And whoever does not receive you nor listen to your words, as you go outside that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.
verses.10:15: Truly I say to you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
verses.10:16: Look, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be prudent as serpents and guileless as doves.
verses.10:17: But be on guard against people, for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;
verses.10:18: and you will even be brought before governors and kings on account of Me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
verses.10:19: But when they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you should speak, for in that hour what you should speak will be given to you;
verses.10:20: for it is not you who are speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.
verses.10:21: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.
verses.10:22: And you will be hated by all because of My name; yet the one who endures to the end, that one will be saved.
verses.10:23: And whenever they persecute you in this city, flee to the next; for truly I say to you, you will by no means finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
verses.10:24: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.
verses.10:25: It is sufficient for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!
verses.10:26: Therefore do not fear them, for nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and hidden that will not be made known.
verses.10:27: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.
verses.10:28: And do not be afraid of those who kill the body yet are unable to kill the soul; rather, fear the One who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
verses.10:29: Are not two sparrows sold for a copper coin? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
verses.10:30: And as for you, even the hairs of your head have all been numbered.
verses.10:31: Therefore do not fear; you are of greater value than many sparrows.
verses.10:32: Everyone, therefore, who will acknowledge Me before people, I also will acknowledge him before My Father who is in heaven;
verses.10:33: but whoever denies Me before people, I also will deny him before My Father who is in heaven.
verses.10:34: Do not suppose that I came to bring peace on the earth; I came not to bring peace, but a sword.
verses.10:35: For I came to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
verses.10:36: and a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.
verses.10:37: The one who loves father or mother above Me is not worthy of Me; and the one who loves son or daughter above Me is not worthy of Me;
verses.10:38: and whoever does not take up his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me.
verses.10:39: The one who has found his life will lose it, and the one who has lost his life on account of Me will find it.
verses.10:40: The one who receives you receives Me, and the one who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
verses.10:41: The one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person's reward.
verses.10:42: And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he will by no means lose his reward."
verses.11:1: And it happened that when Jesus had finished giving instructions to His twelve disciples, He departed from there to teach and to proclaim in their cities.
verses.11:2: Now when John heard in prison about the works of the Christ, he sent word by his disciples
verses.11:3: and said to Him, "Are You the Coming One, or should we expect another?"
verses.11:4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Go and report to John what you hear and see:
verses.11:5: the blind regain sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised and the poor have good news proclaimed to them;
verses.11:6: and blessed is anyone who does not take offense at Me."
verses.11:7: Now as these men were departing, Jesus began to speak to the crowds concerning John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.11:8: Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft garments? Look, those who wear soft garments are in the houses of kings.
verses.11:9: Then why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
verses.11:10: This is the one concerning whom it is written, 'Look, I am sending My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.'
verses.11:11: Truly I say to you, among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
verses.11:12: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent people seize it.
verses.11:13: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John;
verses.11:14: and if you are willing to accept it, he himself is Elijah who is to come.
verses.11:15: The one who has ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.11:16: But to what should I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others
verses.11:17: and say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not lament.'
verses.11:18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
verses.11:19: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look, a gluttonous man and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!' Yet wisdom is vindicated by her works."
verses.11:20: Then He began to reproach the cities in which most of His mighty works had been done, because they did not repent:
verses.11:21: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.11:22: Nevertheless I say to you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
verses.11:23: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will descend to Hades! For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until today.
verses.11:24: Nevertheless I say to you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you."
verses.11:25: At that time Jesus answered and said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that You hid these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to infants;
verses.11:26: yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in Your sight.
verses.11:27: All things were delivered to Me by My Father, and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone fully know the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
verses.11:28: Come to Me, all who toil and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
verses.11:29: Take up My yoke upon you and learn from Me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you will find rest for your souls;
verses.11:30: for My yoke is kindly, and My load is light."
verses.12:1: At that time Jesus walked through the grainfields on the Sabbath; His disciples became hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
verses.12:2: But the Pharisees saw this and said to Him, "Look, Your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath."
verses.12:3: He replied to them, "Have you not read what David did when he became hungry, along with those who were with him,
verses.12:4: how he entered the house of God and they ate the loaves of presentation, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, except for the priests alone?
verses.12:5: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
verses.12:6: Now I say to you that something greater than the temple is here.
verses.12:7: But if you had known what it means, 'I want mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the guiltless.
verses.12:8: For the Son of Man is the Lord of the Sabbath."
verses.12:9: Moving on from there, He went into their synagogue.
verses.12:10: And look, a man was there who had a withered hand. And they questioned Him, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" so that they might accuse Him.
verses.12:11: He said to them, "What man among you who has one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
verses.12:12: How much more valuable, then, is a person than a sheep! Therefore, it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."
verses.12:13: Then He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and it was restored sound, like the other.
verses.12:14: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
verses.12:15: Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Many followed Him, and He healed them all,
verses.12:16: and He warned them strictly not to make Him known,
verses.12:17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.12:18: "Look, My Servant whom I have chosen, My Beloved in whom My soul delights; I will place My Spirit upon Him, and He will announce justice to the nations.
verses.12:19: He will not quarrel nor shout aloud, nor will anyone hear His voice in the streets.
verses.12:20: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish, until He brings justice forth to victory.
verses.12:21: And in His name nations will hope."
verses.12:22: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Him, and He healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
verses.12:23: All the crowds were astounded and were saying, "Could this man be the Son of David?"
verses.12:24: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, "This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons."
verses.12:25: Knowing their thoughts, He said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
verses.12:26: And if Satan casts out Satan, he has become divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?
verses.12:27: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? For this reason, they themselves will be your judges.
verses.12:28: But if by the Spirit of God I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
verses.12:29: Or how can anyone enter the house of the strong man and carry off his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.
verses.12:30: The one who is not with Me is against Me, and the one who does not gather with Me scatters.
verses.12:31: For this reason I say to you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.12:32: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; yet whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the one to come.
verses.12:33: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for from the fruit the tree is known.
verses.12:34: Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things while being evil? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
verses.12:35: The good person brings out good things from the good treasure, and the evil person brings out evil things from the evil treasure.
verses.12:36: Now I say to you that for every idle word people will speak, they will render an account concerning it on the day of judgment;
verses.12:37: for from your words you will be justified, and from your words you will be condemned."
verses.12:38: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered Him, saying, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from You."
verses.12:39: He answered and said to them, "An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, yet no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
verses.12:40: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
verses.12:41: Men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah—and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.12:42: The queen of the South will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to listen to the wisdom of Solomon—and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.12:43: Now when the unclean spirit goes out from a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and finds none.
verses.12:44: Then it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.' And upon arriving, it finds it vacant, swept, and put in order.
verses.12:45: Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and entering in, they settle there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. Thus it will also be with this evil generation."
verses.12:46: While He was still speaking to the crowds, look, His mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to Him.
verses.12:47: Someone said to Him, "Look, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to You."
verses.12:48: But answering, He said to the one who told Him, "Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?"
verses.12:49: And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers!
verses.12:50: For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, that one is My brother and sister and mother."
verses.13:1: On that day Jesus went out from the house and was sitting beside the sea.
verses.13:2: And large crowds gathered to Him, so that He stepped into a boat and sat down, while the whole crowd was standing on the shore.
verses.13:3: And He spoke many things to them in parables, saying, "Look, the sower went out to sow.
verses.13:4: And while he was sowing, some seeds fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured them.
verses.13:5: Others fell on the rocky places, where they did not have much soil, and immediately they sprang up because they had no depth of soil;
verses.13:6: but when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered away.
verses.13:7: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
verses.13:8: Still others fell on the good soil and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty.
verses.13:9: The one who has ears, let him hear."
verses.13:10: And the disciples approached and said to Him, "Why do You speak to them in parables?"
verses.13:11: And He answered and said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
verses.13:12: For whoever has, to him it will be given and he will have in abundance; yet whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
verses.13:13: For this reason I speak to them in parables: because while seeing they do not see, and while hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
verses.13:14: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled, which says, 'Hearing you will hear and by no means understand, and seeing you will see and by no means perceive.
verses.13:15: For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have scarcely heard, and they have closed their eyes; otherwise they might see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.'
verses.13:16: Yet your eyes are blessed because they see, and your ears because they hear.
verses.13:17: For truly I say to you that many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
verses.13:18: You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower.
verses.13:19: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart; this is the one sown along the path.
verses.13:20: And the one sown on the rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy;
verses.13:21: yet he has no root in himself, but is temporary, and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
verses.13:22: And the one sown among the thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.13:23: And the one sown on the good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and produces, one a hundredfold, another sixty, and another thirty."
verses.13:24: He set another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field.
verses.13:25: But while the people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away.
verses.13:26: And when the blade sprouted and produced fruit, then the weeds also appeared.
verses.13:27: And the slaves of the master of the house approached and said to him, 'Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have weeds?'
verses.13:28: And he said to them, 'An enemy has done this.' And the slaves said to him, 'Do you want us, then, to go and gather them?'
verses.13:29: But he said, 'No, otherwise while gathering the weeds you might uproot the wheat along with them.
verses.13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest; and at the time of the harvest I will tell the reapers, "Gather the weeds first and bind them into bundles to burn them up, but gather the wheat into my barn."'"
verses.13:31: He set another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field;
verses.13:32: which is indeed smaller than all the seeds, yet when it has grown, it is larger than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches."
verses.13:33: He spoke another parable to them: "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened."
verses.13:34: All these things Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables, and without a parable He would speak nothing to them,
verses.13:35: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world."
verses.13:36: Then He left the crowds and went into the house. And His disciples approached Him, saying, "Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field."
verses.13:37: And He answered and said, "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
verses.13:38: and the field is the world; and as for the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the weeds are the sons of the evil one,
verses.13:39: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; and the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
verses.13:40: Therefore, just as the weeds are gathered and burned up with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
verses.13:41: The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will gather out of His kingdom all stumbling blocks and those who practice lawlessness,
verses.13:42: and will throw them into the furnace of fire; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:43: Then the righteous will shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. The one who has ears, let him hear.
verses.13:44: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid, and from his joy he goes and sells everything that he has and buys that field.
verses.13:45: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls;
verses.13:46: and upon finding one pearl of great value, he went away and sold everything that he had and bought it.
verses.13:47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering from every kind;
verses.13:48: when it was full, they drew it up onto the shore, and sitting down they gathered the good into containers, but threw the bad away.
verses.13:49: So it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil ones from among the righteous
verses.13:50: and will throw them into the furnace of fire; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:51: Have you understood all these things?" They said to Him, "Yes."
verses.13:52: And He said to them, "Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a house who brings out of his treasury things new and old."
verses.13:53: And it happened that when Jesus had finished these parables, He departed from there.
verses.13:54: And coming to His hometown, He was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, "Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
verses.13:55: Is this not the carpenter's son? Is His mother not called Mary, and His brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
verses.13:56: And His sisters, are they not all with us? Where then did this man get all these things?"
verses.13:57: And they took offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not dishonored except in his hometown and in his household."
verses.13:58: And He did not perform many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
verses.14:1: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus,
verses.14:2: and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he himself has been raised from the dead, and for this reason the miraculous powers are working in him."
verses.14:3: For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him away in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip,
verses.14:4: for John kept saying to him, "It is not lawful for you to have her."
verses.14:5: And although he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they regarded him as a prophet.
verses.14:6: But when Herod's birthday arrived, the daughter of Herodias danced in their midst and pleased Herod,
verses.14:7: so he promised with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.
verses.14:8: Prompted beforehand by her mother, she said, "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
verses.14:9: And the king was grieved; yet because of his oaths and those reclining with him, he commanded that it be given,
verses.14:10: and he sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
verses.14:11: His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she carried it to her mother.
verses.14:12: Then his disciples came, took away the body, and buried him; and they went and reported it to Jesus.
verses.14:13: Now when Jesus heard this, He withdrew from there in a boat to a desolate place by Himself; and when the crowds heard of it, they followed Him on foot from the cities.
verses.14:14: And when He came ashore, He saw a large crowd, and He was moved with compassion for them and healed their sick.
verses.14:15: When evening came, the disciples approached Him, saying, "The place is desolate and the hour has already passed; dismiss the crowds, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves."
verses.14:16: But Jesus said to them, "They have no need to go away; you give them something to eat."
verses.14:17: And they said to Him, "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
verses.14:18: He said, "Bring them to Me here."
verses.14:19: And commanding the crowds to recline on the grass, He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up toward heaven, He spoke a blessing; then breaking the loaves, He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
verses.14:20: And all of them ate and were satisfied, and they picked up what remained of the broken pieces, twelve full baskets.
verses.14:21: Now those who ate were about five thousand men, apart from women and children.
verses.14:22: And immediately He made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
verses.14:23: And after dismissing the crowds, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone.
verses.14:24: Now the boat was already in the middle of the sea, being battered by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
verses.14:25: During the fourth watch of the night, He came to them, walking on the sea.
verses.14:26: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified, saying, "It is a ghost!" And they cried out in fear.
verses.14:27: At once Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Have courage, it is I; do not fear."
verses.14:28: Peter answered Him and said, "Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the waters."
verses.14:29: And He said, "Come." And stepping down from the boat, Peter walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.
verses.14:30: But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, "Lord, save me!"
verses.14:31: And immediately Jesus reached out His hand, grasped him, and said to him, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"
verses.14:32: And when they climbed into the boat, the wind ceased.
verses.14:33: Then those in the boat worshiped Him, saying, "Truly You are God's Son."
verses.14:34: And after crossing over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
verses.14:35: When the men of that place recognized Him, they sent word throughout all that surrounding region and brought to Him all who were ill,
verses.14:36: and they were pleading with Him that they might only touch the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched it were made completely well.
verses.15:1: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying,
verses.15:2: "Why do Your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
verses.15:3: And He answered and said to them, "Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?
verses.15:4: For God commanded, saying, 'Honor father and mother,' and, 'Let the one who speaks evil of father or mother surely die.'
verses.15:5: But you say, 'Whoever says to his father or mother, "Whatever you might gain from me is a gift,"
verses.15:6: he is not to honor his father.' And you have nullified the word of God because of your tradition.
verses.15:7: Hypocrites! Rightly did Isaiah prophesy concerning you, saying,
verses.15:8: 'This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart keeps far from Me;
verses.15:9: yet in vain they worship Me, teaching as teachings the commands of men.'"
verses.15:10: And calling the crowd to Himself, He said to them, "Hear and understand:
verses.15:11: It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth—this defiles a person."
verses.15:12: Then the disciples came and said to Him, "Do You know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard the saying?"
verses.15:13: And He answered and said, "Every plant that My heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
verses.15:14: Leave them alone; they are blind guides. And if a blind man guides a blind man, both will fall into a pit."
verses.15:15: Then Peter answered and said to Him, "Explain the parable to us."
verses.15:16: And He said, "Are you also still without understanding?
verses.15:17: Do you not yet perceive that everything entering into the mouth passes into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine?
verses.15:18: But the things that come out of the mouth come forth from the heart, and those defile a person.
verses.15:19: For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.
verses.15:20: These are the things that defile a person; but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person."
verses.15:21: And going out from there, Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.
verses.15:22: And look, a Canaanite woman came out from that region and was crying out, saying, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is severely demon-possessed."
verses.15:23: But He did not answer her a word. And His disciples came and were urging Him, saying, "Send her away, because she is crying out behind us."
verses.15:24: And He answered and said, "I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
verses.15:25: But she came and bowed down before Him, saying, "Lord, help me."
verses.15:26: And He answered and said, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
verses.15:27: And she said, "Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
verses.15:28: Then Jesus answered and said to her, "Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed from that hour.
verses.15:29: And moving on from there, Jesus came along the Sea of Galilee, and going up onto the mountain, He sat there.
verses.15:30: And large crowds came to Him, having with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others, and they laid them at His feet, and He healed them;
verses.15:31: so that the crowd marveled as they saw the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
verses.15:32: Now Jesus, calling His disciples to Himself, said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because they have remained with Me three days now and do not have anything to eat; and I do not wish to send them away hungry, otherwise they might faint on the way."
verses.15:33: And the disciples said to Him, "Where would we get so many loaves in a desolate place as to satisfy so large a crowd?"
verses.15:34: And Jesus said to them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
verses.15:35: And directing the crowd to recline on the ground,
verses.15:36: He took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks, He broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
verses.15:37: And they all ate and were satisfied; and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets full.
verses.15:38: And those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children.
verses.15:39: And after sending the crowds away, He got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.
verses.16:1: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing Him, they asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.
verses.16:2: And He answered and said to them,
verses.16:3: "⟦And in the morning, 'Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.' You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but the signs of the times you cannot.⟧
verses.16:4: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah." And leaving them, He went away.
verses.16:5: And when the disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
verses.16:6: And Jesus said to them, "Watch and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
verses.16:7: And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "We did not bring bread."
verses.16:8: But Jesus, knowing this, said, "Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread?
verses.16:9: Do you not yet perceive, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
verses.16:10: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many large baskets you took up?
verses.16:11: How is it that you do not perceive that I did not speak to you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
verses.16:12: Then they understood that He had not said to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
verses.16:13: Now when Jesus came into the districts of Caesarea Philippi, He was asking His disciples, saying, "Who do people say that the Son of Man is?"
verses.16:14: And they said, "Some say John the Baptist, and others Elijah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
verses.16:15: He said to them, "But who do you say that I am?"
verses.16:16: And Simon Peter answered and said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
verses.16:17: And Jesus answered and said to him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but My Father who is in heaven.
verses.16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.
verses.16:19: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on the earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on the earth will have been loosed in heaven."
verses.16:20: Then He strictly charged the disciples that they should tell no one that He was the Christ.
verses.16:21: From that time Jesus Christ began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised on the third day.
verses.16:22: And taking Him aside, Peter began to rebuke Him, saying, "Far be it from You, Lord! This will certainly not happen to You."
verses.16:23: But He turned and said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me, because you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men."
verses.16:24: Then Jesus said to His disciples, "If anyone wants to come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
verses.16:25: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of Me will find it.
verses.16:26: For what will a person be profited if he gains the whole world yet forfeits his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
verses.16:27: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to his conduct.
verses.16:28: Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will by no means taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom."
verses.17:1: And after six days, Jesus took along Peter and James and his brother John, and led them up onto a high mountain by themselves.
verses.17:2: And He was transfigured in front of them, and His face shone like the sun, while His garments became white as the light.
verses.17:3: And look, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, conversing with Him.
verses.17:4: Then Peter answered and said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You wish, I will make three tents here—one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.17:5: While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and look, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is My Son, the Beloved, in whom I delight; listen to Him."
verses.17:6: When the disciples heard it, they fell down on their faces and were greatly afraid.
verses.17:7: And Jesus approached, touched them, and said, "Rise, and do not be afraid."
verses.17:8: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus Himself alone.
verses.17:9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, "Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man rises from the dead."
verses.17:10: And His disciples questioned Him, saying, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
verses.17:11: And He answered and said, "Elijah indeed is coming and will restore all things;
verses.17:12: but I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man is also about to suffer from them."
verses.17:13: Then the disciples understood that He had spoken to them concerning John the Baptist.
verses.17:14: And when they came to the crowd, a man approached Him, kneeling before Him
verses.17:15: and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures and suffers badly; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
verses.17:16: And I brought him to Your disciples, and they were not able to heal him."
verses.17:17: And Jesus answered and said, "O unbelieving and twisted generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to Me."
verses.17:18: And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.
verses.17:19: Then the disciples approached Jesus privately and said, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
verses.17:20: And He told them, "Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to over there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."
verses.17:22: Now while they were gathering together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into the hands of men,
verses.17:23: and they will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised." And they were greatly grieved.
verses.17:24: When they came to Capernaum, those who collected the two-drachma tax approached Peter and said, "Does your teacher not pay the two-drachma tax?"
verses.17:25: He said, "Yes." And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs or poll tax? From their own sons, or from strangers?"
verses.17:26: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him, "Then indeed the sons are free.
verses.17:27: Yet so that we do not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you open its mouth, you will find a stater. Take that and give it to them for Me and for you."
verses.18:1: At that hour the disciples approached Jesus, saying, "Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
verses.18:2: And calling a little child to Himself, He set the child in the midst of them
verses.18:3: and said, "Truly I tell you, unless you turn around and become like little children, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:4: Whoever therefore will humble himself like this little child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:5: And whoever welcomes one little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
verses.18:6: But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him that a donkey-turned millstone be hung around his neck and that he be drowned in the depths of the sea.
verses.18:7: Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For it is necessary that stumbling blocks come, yet woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.
verses.18:8: And if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; it is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into the eternal fire.
verses.18:9: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you; it is better for you to enter into life with one eye, than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
verses.18:10: See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I tell you that their angels in heaven continually look upon the face of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:12: What do you think? If any man comes to have a hundred sheep, and one of them strays away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go search for the one that is straying?
verses.18:13: And if it happens that he finds it, truly I tell you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not strayed.
verses.18:14: So it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
verses.18:15: Now if your brother sins, go and show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.
verses.18:16: But if he does not listen, take one or two more along with you, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be confirmed.
verses.18:17: And if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church; and if he also refuses to listen to the church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
verses.18:18: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
verses.18:19: Again, truly I tell you that if two of you agree on earth concerning anything that they may ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:20: For where two or three have been gathered together in My name, there I am in the midst of them."
verses.18:21: Then Peter approached and said to Him, "Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
verses.18:22: Jesus said to him, "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
verses.18:23: For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
verses.18:24: And when he began to settle them, one who owed him ten thousand talents was brought to him.
verses.18:25: Since he did not have the means to repay, the master ordered him to be sold, along with his wife and children and everything that he had, and payment to be made.
verses.18:26: So the servant fell down and bowed before him, saying, 'Master, be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.'
verses.18:27: And moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the loan.
