verses.18:28: But going out, that servant found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay back what you owe.'
verses.18:29: So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you.'
verses.18:30: Yet he was unwilling, and went away and threw him into prison until he should pay back what was owed.
verses.18:31: So when his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved, and came and reported clearly to their master all that had happened.
verses.18:32: Then his master summoned him and said to him, 'You wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me;
verses.18:33: should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I also had mercy on you?'
verses.18:34: And being angry, his master handed him over to the torturers until he should repay all that was owed to him.
verses.18:35: In the same way, My heavenly Father will also do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts."
verses.19:1: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, that He departed from Galilee and came into the territory of Judea beyond the Jordan.
verses.19:2: And many crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
verses.19:3: And Pharisees came up to Him, testing Him and saying, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?"
verses.19:4: And He answered and said, "Have you not read that the One who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
verses.19:5: and said, 'For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh'?
verses.19:6: So then, they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no man separate."
verses.19:7: They said to Him, "Why then did Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and divorce her?"
verses.19:8: He said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart, Moses permitted you to divorce your wives; yet from the beginning it has not been this way.
verses.19:9: And I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
verses.19:10: The disciples said to Him, "If the case of the man with his wife is like this, it is not advantageous to marry."
verses.19:11: And He said to them, "Not all accept this saying, but those to whom it has been given.
verses.19:12: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who is able to accept this, let him accept it."
verses.19:13: Then little children were brought to Him so that He might lay His hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.
verses.19:14: But Jesus said, "Allow the little children, and do not hinder them from coming to Me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."
verses.19:15: And having laid His hands on them, He went on from there.
verses.19:16: And look, someone came up to Him and said, "Teacher, what good thing shall I do so that I may have eternal life?"
verses.19:17: And He said to him, "Why do you ask Me about what is good? There is One who is good. Yet if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments."
verses.19:18: He said to Him, "Which ones?" And Jesus said, "'You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness,
verses.19:19: honor your father and mother,' and, 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'"
verses.19:20: The young man said to Him, "All these things I have kept; what am I still lacking?"
verses.19:21: Jesus said to him, "If you wish to be complete, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.19:22: When the young man heard the saying, he went away grieving, for he had many properties.
verses.19:23: And Jesus said to His disciples, "Truly I say to you that a rich man will enter into the kingdom of heaven with difficulty.
verses.19:24: And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.19:25: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished, saying, "Who then can be saved?"
verses.19:26: And looking closely at them, Jesus said to them, "With men this is impossible, yet with God all things are possible."
verses.19:27: Then Peter answered and said to Him, "Look, we have left everything and followed You; what then will there be for us?"
verses.19:28: And Jesus said to them, "Truly I say to you that you who have followed Me, in the rebirth, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.19:29: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
verses.19:30: Yet many who are first will be last, and last will be first."
verses.20:1: "For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a master of a house, who went out at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard.
verses.20:2: And having agreed with the laborers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
verses.20:3: And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace;
verses.20:4: and to those he said, 'You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.'
verses.20:5: And they went. Going out again about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did likewise.
verses.20:6: And about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and he said to them, 'Why have you been standing here all day idle?'
verses.20:7: They said to him, 'Because no one hired us.' He said to them, 'You also go into the vineyard.'
verses.20:8: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, 'Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.'
verses.20:9: And those from about the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.
verses.20:10: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; yet they themselves also received a denarius each.
verses.20:11: And when they received it, they were grumbling against the master of the house,
verses.20:12: saying, 'These last ones worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.'
verses.20:13: But he answered one of them and said, 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?
verses.20:14: Take what is yours and go; yet I wish to give to this last man just as also to you.
verses.20:15: Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?'
verses.20:16: So the last will be first, and the first, last."
verses.20:17: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside privately, and on the way He said to them,
verses.20:18: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn Him to death,
verses.20:19: and will hand Him over to the Gentiles to mock and flog and crucify Him, and on the third day He will rise."
verses.20:20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came up to Him with her sons, bowing down and asking something from Him.
verses.20:21: And He said to her, "What do you wish?" She said to Him, "Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one on Your right and one on Your left, in Your kingdom."
verses.20:22: But Jesus answered and said, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?" They said to Him, "We are able."
verses.20:23: He said to them, "My cup you will indeed drink, yet to sit on My right and on My left is not Mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by My Father."
verses.20:24: And when the ten heard this, they became indignant about the two brothers.
verses.20:25: But Jesus called them to Himself and said, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them.
verses.20:26: It shall not be this way among you; rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant,
verses.20:27: and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave;
verses.20:28: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom in place of many."
verses.20:29: And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.
verses.20:30: And look, two blind men sitting beside the road, having heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.20:31: And the crowd rebuked them so that they would be silent; yet they cried out all the louder, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.20:32: And stopping, Jesus called them and said, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
verses.20:33: They said to Him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
verses.20:34: And moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they regained their sight and followed Him.
verses.21:1: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
verses.21:2: saying to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up and a colt with her; untie them and bring them to Me.
verses.21:3: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, 'The Lord has need of them,' and immediately he will send them."
verses.21:4: Now this took place in order that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.21:5: "Tell the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your King is coming to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.'"
verses.21:6: So the disciples went and did just as Jesus had directed them;
verses.21:7: they brought the donkey and the colt, and placed their garments on them, and He sat upon them.
verses.21:8: And most of the crowd spread their own garments on the road, while others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
verses.21:9: And the crowds going ahead of Him and those following were shouting, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.21:10: And when He entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up, saying, "Who is this?"
verses.21:11: And the crowds were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee."
verses.21:12: And Jesus entered the temple and drove out all those who were selling and buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who were selling doves,
verses.21:13: and He said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you are making it a cave of robbers."
verses.21:14: And blind and lame people came to Him in the temple, and He healed them.
verses.21:15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the marvelous things that He had done, and the children shouting in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" they became indignant,
verses.21:16: and they said to Him, "Do You hear what these are saying?" And Jesus said to them, "Yes. Have you never read, 'Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies You have prepared praise'?"
verses.21:17: And leaving them, He went out of the city to Bethany and spent the night there.
verses.21:18: Now early in the morning, as He was returning to the city, He became hungry.
verses.21:19: And seeing a single fig tree beside the road, He went up to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone. And He said to it, "May fruit never again come from you forever." And instantly the fig tree withered.
verses.21:20: And when the disciples saw this, they were amazed, saying, "How did the fig tree wither instantly?"
verses.21:21: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
verses.21:22: And everything that you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive."
verses.21:23: And when He had entered the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to Him while He was teaching, saying, "By what authority are You doing these things? And who gave You this authority?"
verses.21:24: And Jesus answered and said to them, "I will also ask you one question; if you tell Me that, then I will also tell you by what authority I am doing these things:
verses.21:25: The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?" And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say to us, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
verses.21:26: But if we say, 'From men,' we fear the crowd, for they all regard John as a prophet."
verses.21:27: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know." He also said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
verses.21:28: Now what do you think? A man had two children; and approaching the first, he said, 'Child, go work today in the vineyard.'
verses.21:29: And he answered and said, 'I do not want to,' but afterward he changed his mind and went.
verses.21:30: And approaching the other, he said the same thing; and he answered and said, 'I will, sir,' and he did not go.
verses.21:31: Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
verses.21:32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, whereas the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and you, when you saw this, did not change your minds afterward so as to believe him.
verses.21:33: Listen to another parable. There was a man who was a landowner, who planted a vineyard, and placed a fence around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and leased it out to tenants, and went away on a journey.
verses.21:34: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the tenants to collect his fruits.
verses.21:35: And the tenants seized his slaves: one they beat, another they killed, and another they stoned.
verses.21:36: Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
verses.21:37: Afterward he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.21:38: But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance.'
verses.21:39: So they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
verses.21:40: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
verses.21:41: They said to Him, "He will bring wretched ruin on those wretched men, and he will lease out the vineyard to other tenants who will deliver to him the fruits in their seasons."
verses.21:42: Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures, 'The stone that the builders rejected—this has become the cornerstone; this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?
verses.21:43: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits.
verses.21:44: And the one who falls on this stone will be shattered; and on whomever it falls, it will crush him to dust."
verses.21:45: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard His parables, they realized that He was speaking about them.
verses.21:46: And although they were seeking to seize Him, they feared the crowds, because they regarded Him as a prophet.
verses.22:1: And answering, Jesus again spoke to them in parables, saying,
verses.22:2: "The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man, a king, who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
verses.22:3: And he sent out his slaves to summon those who had been invited to the wedding banquet, and they were unwilling to come.
verses.22:4: Again he sent out other slaves, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited: Look, I have prepared my feast; my bulls and the fattened livestock have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.'
verses.22:5: But paying no attention, they went away, one to his own field and another to his business;
verses.22:6: and the rest seized his slaves, mistreated them, and killed them.
verses.22:7: Then the king became angry, and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers and set their city on fire.
verses.22:8: Then he said to his slaves, 'The wedding banquet is ready, yet those who were invited were not worthy.
verses.22:9: Go therefore to the main intersections of the roads, and invite to the wedding banquet as many as you find.'
verses.22:10: And going out into the roads, those slaves gathered together everyone whom they found, both evil and good; and the wedding banquet was filled with reclining guests.
verses.22:11: But when the king came in to view the reclining guests, he saw a man there who was not wearing a wedding garment.
verses.22:12: And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here not having a wedding garment?' And he was struck silent.
verses.22:13: Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his feet and hands and cast him out into the outer darkness; in that place there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.'
verses.22:14: For many are called, yet few are chosen."
verses.22:15: Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel on how they might trap Him in speech.
verses.22:16: And they sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and You are not concerned about anyone, for You do not look at the face of people.
verses.22:17: Tell us therefore what You think: Is it lawful to pay a poll tax to Caesar, or not?"
verses.22:18: But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, "Why are you testing Me, hypocrites?
verses.22:19: Show Me the coin of the poll tax." And they brought Him a denarius.
verses.22:20: And He said to them, "Whose is this image and inscription?"
verses.22:21: They said, "Caesar's." Then He said to them, "Pay back therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God."
verses.22:22: And when they heard this, they marveled; and leaving Him, they went away.
verses.22:23: On that day Sadducees came to Him, saying that there is no resurrection, and they questioned Him,
verses.22:24: saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If someone dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'
verses.22:25: Now there were seven brothers among us; and the first married and died, and having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother.
verses.22:26: Likewise also the second and the third, through all seven.
verses.22:27: And after all of them, the woman died.
verses.22:28: In the resurrection, therefore, of which of the seven will she be the wife? For they all had her."
verses.22:29: But answering, Jesus said to them, "You are in error, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.
verses.22:30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
verses.22:31: Now concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying,
verses.22:32: 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
verses.22:33: And when the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.
verses.22:34: Now when the Pharisees heard that He had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together in one place.
verses.22:35: And one of them, an expert in the law, questioned Him, testing Him:
verses.22:36: "Teacher, which commandment is greatest in the law?"
verses.22:37: And He said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.
verses.22:38: This is the great and first commandment.
verses.22:39: And a second is similar to it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
verses.22:40: On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets."
verses.22:41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
verses.22:42: saying, "What do you think concerning the Christ? Whose son is He?" They said to Him, "David's."
verses.22:43: He said to them, "How then does David in the Spirit call Him 'Lord,' saying,
verses.22:44: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I place Your enemies beneath Your feet'?
verses.22:45: If David then calls Him 'Lord,' how is He his son?"
verses.22:46: And no one was able to answer Him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to question Him any longer.
verses.23:1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples,
verses.23:2: saying, "On the seat of Moses the scribes and the Pharisees have sat down.
verses.23:3: Therefore do and keep everything that they tell you, but do not act according to their deeds, for they speak and do not act.
verses.23:4: And they bind up burdens heavy and hard to carry and place them on people's shoulders, yet they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger.
verses.23:5: And they do all their deeds in order to be seen by people; for they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the tassels,
verses.23:6: and they love the foremost place at banquets and the foremost seats in the synagogues,
verses.23:7: and the greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called by people, 'Rabbi.'
verses.23:8: But you, do not be called 'Rabbi,' for one is your instructor, and all of you are brothers.
verses.23:9: And do not call anyone on the earth your father, for one is your heavenly Father.
verses.23:10: Nor be called instructors, because your instructor is one, the Christ.
verses.23:11: But the greatest among you will be your servant.
verses.23:12: And whoever lifts himself up will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be lifted up.
verses.23:13: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before people; for you yourselves do not enter, nor do you permit those who are entering to enter.
verses.23:15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you traverse the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
verses.23:16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is obligated.'
verses.23:17: Fools and blind! For which is greater, the gold, or the sanctuary that sanctified the gold?
verses.23:18: And, 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it is obligated.'
verses.23:19: Fools and blind! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
verses.23:20: Therefore the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by all things on it;
verses.23:21: and the one who swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by Him who dwells in it;
verses.23:22: and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by Him who sits upon it.
verses.23:23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law—justice and mercy and faithfulness; yet it was necessary to do these and not to neglect those.
verses.23:24: Blind guides, straining out the gnat yet swallowing the camel!
verses.23:25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, yet inside they are full of robbery and self-indulgence.
verses.23:26: Blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that the outside of them may also become clean.
verses.23:27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you resemble whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, yet inside are full of bones of the dead and all uncleanness;
verses.23:28: so you also outwardly appear righteous to people, yet inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
verses.23:29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
verses.23:30: and say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been participants with them in the blood of the prophets.'
verses.23:31: Consequently you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.23:32: And you, fill up the measure of your fathers.
verses.23:33: Serpents, offspring of vipers, how can you escape from the judgment of Gehenna?
verses.23:34: Because of this, look, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
verses.23:35: so that all the righteous blood shed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.23:36: Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.23:37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her—how often I wanted to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling!
verses.23:38: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
verses.23:39: For I say to you, from now on you will certainly not see Me until you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
verses.24:1: And leaving the temple, Jesus was going on His way, and His disciples approached to show Him the buildings of the temple.
verses.24:2: But He answered and said to them, "Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, by no means will a stone be left here upon a stone that will not be torn down."
verses.24:3: Now while He was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached Him privately, saying, "Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the close of the age?"
verses.24:4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Watch out that no one leads you astray.
verses.24:5: For many will come in My name, saying, 'I am the Christ,' and they will lead many astray.
verses.24:6: And you are going to hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for it must take place, but the end is not yet.
verses.24:7: For nation will rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
verses.24:8: But all these things are the beginning of labor pains.
verses.24:9: Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of My name.
verses.24:10: And then many will fall away, and they will hand one another over and hate one another.
verses.24:11: And many false prophets will rise up and lead many astray.
verses.24:12: And because lawlessness will multiply, the love of the many will grow cold.
verses.24:13: Yet the one who perseveres to the end, that one will be saved.
verses.24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
verses.24:15: Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation that was spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
verses.24:16: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
verses.24:17: let the one on the housetop not go down to take the things out of his house,
verses.24:18: and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
verses.24:19: And woe to the women who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
verses.24:20: And pray that your flight will not take place in winter or on a Sabbath.
verses.24:21: For then there will be great affliction, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, nor will by any means occur again.
verses.24:22: And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be cut short.
verses.24:23: Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!' or 'Here!' do not believe it.
verses.24:24: For false christs and false prophets will rise up and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
verses.24:25: See, I have told you beforehand.
verses.24:26: Therefore, if they say to you, 'Look, He is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, He is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it.
verses.24:27: For just as lightning comes out from the east and shines all the way to the west, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.
verses.24:28: Wherever the carcass is, there the vultures will be gathered together.
verses.24:29: And immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its radiance, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
verses.24:30: And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
verses.24:31: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet, and they will gather together His chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
verses.24:32: Now learn the parable from the fig tree: whenever its branch has already become tender and sprouts leaves, you know that summer is near.
verses.24:33: In the same way, you also, when you see all these things, know that He is near, at the doors.
verses.24:34: Truly I tell you, this generation will by no means pass away until all these things take place.
verses.24:35: Heaven and earth will pass away, yet My words will by no means pass away.
verses.24:36: But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of the heavens nor the Son, except the Father alone.
verses.24:37: For just as the days of Noah were, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.
verses.24:38: For just as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark,
verses.24:39: and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away—so also the coming of the Son of Man will be.
verses.24:40: Then two men will be in the field; one is taken and one is left.
verses.24:41: Two women will be grinding at the mill; one is taken and one is left.
verses.24:42: Stay awake, therefore, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
verses.24:43: But know this: if the householder had known during which watch the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.24:44: For this reason you also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
verses.24:45: Who then is the faithful and sensible slave whom the master put in charge of his household to give them their food at the proper time?
verses.24:46: Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he arrives, will find doing so.
verses.24:47: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
verses.24:48: But if that wicked slave says in his heart, 'My master is taking a long time,'
verses.24:49: and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with drunkards,
verses.24:50: the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know,
verses.24:51: and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.25:1: "Then the kingdom of heaven will be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
verses.25:2: Now five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
verses.25:3: For when the foolish ones took their lamps, they took no oil with them;
verses.25:4: but the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their own lamps.
verses.25:5: Now while the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and were sleeping.
verses.25:6: But at midnight a cry rang out: 'Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!'
verses.25:7: Then all those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.
verses.25:8: And the foolish ones said to the wise ones, 'Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.'
verses.25:9: But the wise ones answered, saying, 'No, there will certainly not be enough for us and for you; go rather to those who sell and buy for yourselves.'
verses.25:10: And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
verses.25:11: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, 'Lord, lord, open to us!'
verses.25:12: But he answered and said, 'Truly I say to you, I do not know you.'
verses.25:13: Stay awake, therefore, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
verses.25:14: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his own servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
verses.25:15: To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he went on his journey. Immediately
verses.25:16: the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained five more talents.
verses.25:17: In the same way, the one with the two also gained two more.
verses.25:18: But the one who had received the one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master's money.
verses.25:19: Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
verses.25:20: And the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought five more talents, saying, 'Master, you entrusted five talents to me; look, I have gained five more talents.'
verses.25:21: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful over a few things; I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:22: The one with the two talents also came forward and said, 'Master, you entrusted two talents to me; look, I have gained two more talents.'
verses.25:23: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful over a few things; I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:24: Then the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, 'Master, I knew you, that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter;
verses.25:25: and being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.'
verses.25:26: But his master answered and said to him, 'Wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?
verses.25:27: Therefore you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and upon returning I would have received back what is mine with interest.
verses.25:28: Therefore take the talent away from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
verses.25:29: For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will abound; yet from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
verses.25:30: And throw the worthless servant out into the outer darkness; in that place there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.'
verses.25:31: Now when the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His glory.
verses.25:32: And all the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, just as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats;
verses.25:33: and He will place the sheep on His right, but the goats on the left.
verses.25:34: Then the King will say to those on His right, 'Come, you blessed ones of My Father, inherit the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
verses.25:35: For I was hungry and you gave Me food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave Me a drink; I was a stranger and you took Me in;
verses.25:36: naked, and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me.'
verses.25:37: Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You a drink?
verses.25:38: And when did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?
verses.25:39: And when did we see You sick or in prison and come to You?'
verses.25:40: And answering, the King will say to them, 'Truly I say to you, to the degree that you did it to one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did it to Me.'
verses.25:41: Then He will also say to those on the left, 'Depart from Me, accursed ones, into the eternal fire that has been prepared for the devil and his angels.
verses.25:42: For I was hungry and you did not give Me food to eat; I was thirsty and you did not give Me a drink;
verses.25:43: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in; naked, and you did not clothe Me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit Me.'
verses.25:44: Then they themselves will also answer, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve You?'
verses.25:45: Then He will answer them, saying, 'Truly I say to you, to the degree that you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.'
verses.25:46: And these will depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."
verses.26:1: And it happened when Jesus finished all these words, He said to His disciples,
verses.26:2: "You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."
verses.26:3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered together in the courtyard of the high priest who was called Caiaphas,
verses.26:4: and they took counsel together so that they might seize Jesus by deceit and kill Him.
verses.26:5: But they were saying, "Not during the festival, so that an uproar may not occur among the people."
verses.26:6: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
verses.26:7: a woman came up to Him having an alabaster flask of very costly perfume, and she poured it out upon His head as He reclined at table.
verses.26:8: But when the disciples saw this, they became indignant, saying, "Why this waste?
verses.26:9: For this could have been sold for a high price and given to the poor."
verses.26:10: But Jesus, knowing this, said to them, "Why do you cause trouble for the woman? For she has done a good work for Me.
verses.26:11: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.
verses.26:12: For by pouring this perfume on My body, she did it to prepare Me for burial.
verses.26:13: Truly I say to you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of in memory of her."
verses.26:14: Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
verses.26:15: and said, "What are you willing to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?" And they weighed out to him thirty pieces of silver.
verses.26:16: And from that time he was seeking a good opportunity to hand Him over.
verses.26:17: Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came up to Jesus, saying, "Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?"
verses.26:18: And He said, "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house with My disciples.'"
verses.26:19: And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.26:20: Now when evening came, He was reclining at table with the twelve,
verses.26:21: and as they were eating, He said, "Truly I say to you that one of you will hand Me over."
verses.26:22: And being deeply grieved, each one began to say to Him, "Surely it is not I, Lord?"
verses.26:23: And He answered and said, "The one who dipped his hand with Me in the dish, this one will hand Me over.
verses.26:24: The Son of Man indeed goes just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.26:25: Then Judas, the one handing Him over, answered and said, "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?" He said to him, "You have said it."
verses.26:26: Now while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed it, He broke it, and giving it to the disciples, He said, "Take, eat; this is My body."
verses.26:27: And taking a cup and having given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you,
verses.26:28: for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out on behalf of many for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.26:29: But I say to you, from now on I will certainly not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father."
verses.26:30: And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.26:31: Then Jesus said to them, "All of you will stumble because of Me on this night, for it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
verses.26:32: But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
verses.26:33: And Peter answered and said to Him, "Though all will stumble because of You, I will never stumble."
verses.26:34: Jesus said to him, "Truly I say to you that on this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times."
verses.26:35: Peter said to Him, "Even if I must die with You, I will certainly not deny You." All the disciples also spoke in the same way.
verses.26:36: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and He said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
verses.26:37: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to be grieved and in anguish.
verses.26:38: Then He said to them, "My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death; remain here and keep watch with Me."
verses.26:39: And going a little farther, He fell on His face, praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from Me; yet not as I will, but as You do."
verses.26:40: And He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and He said to Peter, "So, were you unable to keep watch with Me for one hour?
verses.26:41: Keep watch and pray so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit indeed is eager, but the flesh is weak."
verses.26:42: Again, a second time, He went away and prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cannot pass away unless I drink it, let Your will be done."
verses.26:43: And coming again, He found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down.
verses.26:44: And leaving them again, He went away and prayed a third time, saying the same words once again.
verses.26:45: Then He came to the disciples and said to them, "Sleep on now and take your rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
verses.26:46: Get up, let us go! Look, the one handing Me over has drawn near."
verses.26:47: And while He was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.
verses.26:48: Now the one handing Him over had given them a sign, saying, "The one whom I kiss, He is the one; seize Him."
verses.26:49: And immediately coming up to Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
verses.26:50: And Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you have come for." Then they came up, laid hands on Jesus, and seized Him.
verses.26:51: And look, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, cut off his ear.
verses.26:52: Then Jesus said to him, "Return your sword to its place, for all who take up a sword will perish by a sword.
verses.26:53: Or do you suppose that I cannot appeal to My Father, and He will immediately place at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
verses.26:54: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen in this way?"
verses.26:55: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to arrest Me? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me.
verses.26:56: But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets may be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left Him and fled.
verses.26:57: Now those who had seized Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered together.
verses.26:58: But Peter was following Him at a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside, he sat with the officers to see the outcome.
verses.26:59: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put Him to death,
verses.26:60: and they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. But later two came forward
verses.26:61: and said, "This man stated, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and build it within three days.'"
verses.26:62: And standing up, the high priest said to Him, "Do You answer nothing? What is it that these men are testifying against You?"
verses.26:63: But Jesus kept silent. And the high priest said to Him, "I put You under oath by the living God that You tell us whether You are the Christ, the Son of God."
verses.26:64: Jesus said to him, "You have said it. Yet I say to you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven."
verses.26:65: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy!
verses.26:66: What do you think?" And they answered and said, "He is deserving of death."
verses.26:67: Then they spat in His face and beat Him with their fists, and others slapped Him,
verses.26:68: saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is the one who struck You?"
verses.26:69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. And a servant girl came up to him, saying, "You also were with Jesus the Galilean."
verses.26:70: But he denied it before everyone, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."
verses.26:71: And as he went out to the gateway, another woman saw him and said to those who were there, "This man was with Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.26:72: And again he denied it with an oath, "I do not know the man."
verses.26:73: And after a little while, those who were standing there came up and said to Peter, "Truly you also are one of them, for even your way of speaking gives you away."
verses.26:74: Then he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know the man." And immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.26:75: And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken, "Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." And going outside, he wept bitterly.
verses.27:1: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus so as to put Him to death;
verses.27:2: and having bound Him, they led Him away and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
verses.27:3: Then Judas, who had betrayed Him, seeing that He had been condemned, was filled with remorse and returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
verses.27:4: saying, "I have sinned in betraying innocent blood." But they said, "What is that to us? You see to it."
verses.27:5: And throwing the silver coins into the sanctuary, he withdrew; and going away, he hanged himself.
verses.27:6: But the chief priests, taking the silver coins, said, "It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood."
verses.27:7: And after taking counsel, they bought with them the Potter's Field for the burial of strangers.
verses.27:8: For that reason, that field has been called Field of Blood until today.
verses.27:9: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, "And they took the thirty silver coins, the price of the One who had been priced, whom some of the sons of Israel priced,
verses.27:10: and they gave them for the potter's field, just as the Lord instructed me."
verses.27:11: Now Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor questioned Him, saying, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him, "You say so."
verses.27:12: And while He was being accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing.
verses.27:13: Then Pilate said to Him, "Do You not hear how many things they are testifying against You?"
verses.27:14: And He did not answer him regarding even a single word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
verses.27:15: Now at each feast, the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd, whichever one they wanted.
verses.27:16: And at that time they had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.
verses.27:17: Therefore, when they had gathered together, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you want me to release to you, Barabbas or Jesus who is called Christ?"
verses.27:18: For he knew that they had handed Him over out of envy.
verses.27:19: Now while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, "Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for today I have suffered many things in a dream because of Him."
verses.27:20: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
verses.27:21: And the governor answered and said to them, "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?" And they said, "Barabbas."
verses.27:22: Pilate said to them, "What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?" All of them said, "Let Him be crucified!"
verses.27:23: But he said, "Why, what evil did He do?" Yet they kept crying out all the more, saying, "Let Him be crucified!"
verses.27:24: Now when Pilate saw that he was achieving nothing, but rather an uproar was starting, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, "I am innocent of this blood; you see to it yourselves."
verses.27:25: And all the people answered and said, "His blood be upon us and upon our children!"
verses.27:26: Then he released Barabbas to them; but after flogging Jesus, he handed Him over to be crucified.
verses.27:27: Then the governor's soldiers, taking Jesus into the Praetorium, gathered the entire cohort around Him.
verses.27:28: And having stripped Him, they put a scarlet cloak around Him,
verses.27:29: and weaving a crown of thorns, they set it on His head, and a reed in His right hand; and kneeling down before Him, they mocked Him, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
verses.27:30: And spitting on Him, they took the reed and kept striking Him on the head.
verses.27:31: And when they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the cloak, put His garments on Him, and led Him away to crucify Him.
verses.27:32: Now as they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene, Simon by name; this man they pressed into service to carry His cross.
verses.27:33: And arriving at a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull,
verses.27:34: they gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink; and having tasted it, He would not drink.
verses.27:35: And after crucifying Him, they divided His garments among themselves, casting lots,
verses.27:36: and sitting down, they were keeping watch over Him there.
verses.27:37: And they placed above His head the written charge against Him: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
verses.27:38: Then two bandits were crucified with Him, one on the right and one on the left.
verses.27:39: And those passing by were reviling Him, shaking their heads
verses.27:40: and saying, "You who destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross."
verses.27:41: Likewise, the chief priests also, mocking Him together with the scribes and elders, were saying,
verses.27:42: "He saved others; He is unable to save Himself. He is King of Israel; let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
verses.27:43: He has trusted in God; let Him deliver Him now, if He delights in Him; for He said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
verses.27:44: In the same way, the bandits who had been crucified with Him were also reproaching Him.
verses.27:45: Now from the sixth hour, darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
verses.27:46: And around the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" that is, "My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?"
verses.27:47: And some of those standing there, hearing this, were saying, "This man is calling Elijah."
verses.27:48: And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and offered Him a drink.
verses.27:49: But the rest were saying, "Leave Him alone; let us see whether Elijah is coming to save Him."
verses.27:50: And Jesus, crying out again in a loud voice, gave up His spirit.
verses.27:51: And look, the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom; and the earth quaked, and the rocks were split,
verses.27:52: and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who were asleep were raised,
verses.27:53: and having come out of the tombs after His resurrection, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
verses.27:54: Now the centurion and those with him who were keeping watch over Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that took place, were greatly terrified, saying, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
verses.27:55: And many women were there watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving Him.
verses.27:56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
verses.27:57: Now when evening had come, a rich man from Arimathea arrived, named Joseph, who himself had also become a disciple of Jesus.
verses.27:58: This man approached Pilate and requested the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given over.
verses.27:59: And taking the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
verses.27:60: and placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock; and having rolled a large stone against the doorway of the tomb, he departed.
verses.27:61: Now Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
verses.27:62: Now on the following day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together before Pilate,
verses.27:63: saying, "Sir, we remembered how that deceiver said while still alive, 'After three days I will be raised.'
verses.27:64: Therefore, order the tomb to be secured until the third day, so that His disciples do not come and steal Him and say to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead,' and the last deception will be worse than the first."
verses.27:65: And Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go and secure it as you know how."
verses.27:66: So they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone along with the guard.
verses.28:1: Now after the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the grave.
verses.28:2: And look, a great earthquake occurred, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came near, rolled away the stone, and was sitting on top of it.
verses.28:3: And his appearance was like lightning, and his garment white as snow.
verses.28:4: And from fear of him the guards were shaken and became like dead men.
verses.28:5: And answering, the angel said to the women, "As for you, do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus, the One who was crucified.
verses.28:6: He is not here, for He has been raised, just as He said. Come here and see the place where He was lying.
verses.28:7: And go quickly and tell His disciples, 'He has been raised from the dead, and look, He is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see Him.' Look, I have told you."
verses.28:8: And departing quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to report to His disciples.
verses.28:9: And look, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings!" And coming near, they grasped His feet and worshiped Him.
verses.28:10: Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and report to My brothers to depart into Galilee, and there they will see Me."
verses.28:11: Now while they were on their way, look, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all the things that had happened.
verses.28:12: And when they had assembled with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
verses.28:13: saying, "Say, 'His disciples came by night and stole Him while we were sleeping.'
verses.28:14: And if this is heard before the governor, we will win him over and make you free from concern."
verses.28:15: And taking the silver, they did as they were instructed. And this report was spread widely among the Jews to this very day.
verses.28:16: Now the eleven disciples journeyed into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them,
verses.28:17: and seeing Him, they worshiped, yet some doubted.
verses.28:18: And Jesus came near and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and upon the earth.
verses.28:19: Therefore, go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
verses.28:20: teaching them to keep everything that I commanded you. And look, I am with you all the days, until the completion of the age."

notes.1:1: Greek "biblos geneseos" ("book of origin/lineage") echoes the Septuagint of Genesis 2:4 and 5:1, introducing Jesus' genealogy as the beginning of a new era.
notes.1:7: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "Asaph" here (and in 1:8) rather than King Asa, and similarly "Amos" in 1:10 rather than King Amon; later manuscripts assimilate both names to the Old Testament kings.
notes.1:21: The name Jesus (Hebrew Yeshua) means "the Lord saves," grounding the angel's declaration that He will save His people from their sins.
notes.1:25: "Did not know her" preserves the biblical idiom for marital relations (in the imperfect tense); the critical Greek text reads simply "a son" without "her firstborn" found in later manuscripts.
notes.2:2: The Greek phrase "en te anatole" ("in the east") can also be understood astronomically as "at its rising."
notes.2:15: Matthew quotes Hosea 11:1, originally spoken of Israel's exodus from Egypt, applying it typologically to Jesus as God's Son.
notes.2:23: No single Old Testament passage contains these exact words; citing "the prophets" collectively, Matthew likely draws on wordplay with Hebrew "netser" ("branch," Isa 11:1) and/or prophetic themes of the Messiah's humble origins.
notes.3:11: The preposition "in" ("in water," "in the Holy Spirit and fire") can also be rendered instrumentally as "with"; "fire" is variously taken to signify purifying refinement or eschatological judgment (compare 3:10, 12).
notes.3:15: "Fulfill all righteousness" refers to carrying out God's saving will and covenant plan in full, here through Jesus' solidarity with John's baptism.
notes.3:16: The critical Greek text reads simply "the heavens were opened," without the addition "to Him" found in some manuscripts.
notes.4:5: Greek pterygion literally means "little wing" and here refers to a high parapet, wing, or turret of the temple complex, traditionally rendered "pinnacle."
notes.4:12: Greek paredothe literally means "was handed over" (i.e., arrested or delivered into custody), the same verb Matthew uses later for Jesus being handed over.
notes.4:15: Greek hodon thalasses ("the way of the sea") reflects a Hebrew phrase meaning "toward the sea" or referring to the major trade route; Greek ton ethnon can be translated either "of the nations" or "of the Gentiles."
notes.4:24: Greek seleniazomenous literally means "moonstruck," an ancient term for people experiencing epilepsy or seizures.
notes.5:22: Raca is an Aramaic term of contempt meaning roughly 'empty-headed.' The critical Greek text omits 'without cause' after 'angry with his brother,' and Gehenna refers to the Valley of Hinnom as an image of final judgment.
notes.5:26: A quadrans was a small Roman bronze coin equal to one-fourth of an assarion, representing a trivial sum.
notes.5:32: The Greek noun porneia covers unlawful sexual conduct broadly, and the passive infinitive moicheuthenai literally conveys causing her to be made an adulteress (or subjected to adultery).
notes.5:37: The Greek phrase tou ponerou may be read as masculine ('the evil one') or neuter ('evil').
notes.5:48: The Greek adjective teleioi ('complete' or 'perfect') carries the sense of moral wholeness, maturity, and undivided devotion.
notes.6:1: The earliest manuscripts read δικαιοσύνην ("righteousness"), whereas later manuscripts harmonize with 6:2 by reading ἐλεημοσύνην ("charitable giving").
notes.6:11: The rare Greek adjective ἐπιούσιον ("daily") is debated in meaning; scholars also propose "necessary for existence" or "for the coming day."
notes.6:13: Greek τοῦ πονηροῦ may be taken as masculine ("the evil one") or neuter ("evil"). The liturgical doxology ("For Yours is the kingdom...") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and from this Greek text.
notes.6:22: In Jewish idiom, a "sound" or "single" eye (ἁπλοῦς) signifies generosity and undivided devotion, contrasting with a "bad" or "evil" eye (πονηρός, 6:23), which signifies greed or envy.
notes.6:27: Greek ἡλικίαν can mean either "lifespan" (with "cubit" used metaphorically for a brief measure of time) or physical "stature."
notes.7:6: "What is holy" (τὸ ἅγιον) alludes to sacrificial meat set apart for God and is used metaphorically for sacred truth or teaching.
notes.7:14: The Greek text reads ὅτι ("for"), while some manuscripts read τί ("how narrow is the gate!"). Greek τεθλιμμένη ("constricted") literally means pressed or hemmed in.
notes.7:17: Greek σαπρὸν ("diseased") literally denotes what is rotten, decayed, or unfit, contrasting with ἀγαθὸν ("good").
notes.8:6: Greek pais can mean either 'servant' or 'boy/son'; in light of the parallel in Luke 7:2 (doulos), 'servant' is preferred here.
notes.8:7: Because the Greek pronoun ego ('I') is emphatic, some scholars read Jesus' words as a question: 'Am I to come and heal him?'
notes.8:24: Greek seismos literally denotes a violent shaking or quake, here used for a fierce storm churning the sea.
notes.8:28: Manuscripts vary among 'Gadarenes' (the earliest reading in Matthew), 'Gerasenes,' and 'Gergesenes.'
notes.9:4: The critical text reads idon ('seeing') rather than the variant eidos ('knowing'), vividly depicting Jesus perceiving their thoughts.
notes.9:15: 'Sons of the bridal chamber' is a Semitic idiom referring to the wedding guests or attendants of the bridegroom.
notes.9:21: Greek sozo ('save') is used here and in v. 22 in the sense of physical healing and restoration ('be made well').
notes.9:34: This verse is omitted in Codex Bezae (D) and some Old Latin witnesses, though it is strongly attested in the primary Alexandrian and Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.9:36: Greek eskylmenoi kai errimmenoi literally means 'troubled/harassed and cast down,' vividly portraying a neglected and vulnerable crowd.
notes.10:4: "Cananaean" transliterates Greek Καναναῖος, derived from an Aramaic term meaning "zealous one" or "Zealot" (cf. Luke 6:15), not a resident of Cana or Canaan.
notes.10:23: "Finish going through" renders Greek τελέσητε ("complete"), referring to completing the mission circuit through Israel's towns; interpreters debate whether the coming of the Son of Man refers to His resurrection vindication, the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70, or His final return.
notes.10:28: "Gehenna" transliterates Greek γέεννα (from the Hebrew Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem), used in Jewish and early Christian usage as a term for final divine judgment and hell.
notes.10:29: "Copper coin" translates Greek ἀσσάριον (assarion), a small Roman bronze coin worth one-sixteenth of a denarius; "apart from your Father" literally renders ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν, conveying without His knowledge or will.
notes.11:12: Greek βιάζεται is debated: taken as passive, the kingdom "suffers violence" from hostile opponents (βιασταί); taken as middle, the kingdom "advances forcefully" and ardent seekers lay hold of it.
notes.11:15: The Saints Greek Critical Text retains ἀκούειν ("to hear"), which is omitted in some early manuscripts.
notes.11:19: "Works" (ἔργων) forms an intentional link back to "the works of the Christ" in 11:2; some manuscripts, harmonizing with Luke 7:35, read "children" (τέκνων).
notes.11:30: "Kindly" renders Greek χρηστός, meaning good, gentle, or easy to bear, as of a well-fitted yoke.
notes.12:4: The Greek verb ephagon ("they ate") is plural in the earliest manuscripts, including David's companions, whereas later manuscripts harmonize it to the singular "he ate." "Loaves of presentation" literally renders tous artous tes protheseos, the consecrated bread set out in the sanctuary (1 Sam 21:1-6).
notes.12:6: The Greek adjective meizon ("something greater") is neuter rather than masculine, pointing broadly to the greater reality of Jesus's messianic ministry and kingdom; the same neuter construction recurs with pleion in 12:41-42.
notes.12:20: Matthew's quotation of Isaiah 42:3 renders the closing phrase as "to victory" (eis nikos), differing from the standard Hebrew ("in truth") and Septuagint wording to highlight the triumphant outcome of the Servant's justice.
notes.12:40: Greek ketos refers to a huge sea creature or sea monster, echoing the Septuagint rendering of the "great fish" in Jonah 2:1.
notes.12:47: This verse is omitted by several important early manuscripts (such as original Sinaiticus and Vaticanus), likely through an accidental scribal skip between the identical endings lalesai ("to speak") in verses 46 and 47.
notes.13:25: Greek zizania refers to bearded darnel (Lolium temulentum), a noxious weed that closely resembles wheat until the grain heads appear.
notes.13:33: Greek sata tria ("three seahs") denotes a dry measure of roughly 36 to 40 liters of flour, enough to feed a large gathering.
notes.13:35: Quoting Psalm 78:2. While the critical text reads "through the prophet" and includes "of the world," a few ancient manuscripts specify "Isaiah" and some omit "of the world."
notes.13:55: Greek tekton denotes a skilled craftsman or builder who worked with wood, stone, or metal, traditionally rendered "carpenter."
notes.14:9: The Greek text uses two finite verbs (was grieved ... commanded) without a conjunction linking them, rather than the participial construction found in some manuscripts. The plural 'oaths' likely emphasizes the solemnity or repeated nature of Herod's pledge.
notes.14:24: The Greek text reads 'was already in the middle of the sea,' whereas several ancient manuscripts read 'was already many stadia away from the land.'
notes.14:27: The phrase 'it is I' literally translates Greek 'ego eimi' ('I am'), which serves both as a normal self-identification and as an echo of God's self-revelation in the Greek Old Testament (e.g., Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 43:10).
notes.14:29: The Greek text reads the finite verb 'and came,' whereas some early manuscripts read the infinitive 'to come.'
notes.14:36: 'Fringe' (Greek 'kraspedon') refers to the tassel attached to the corner of a Jewish outer garment in accordance with the Mosaic Law (Numbers 15:38-39; Deuteronomy 22:12).
notes.15:5: Greek Doron ("gift") refers to a vowed sacred offering dedicated to God (called "Corban" in Mark 7:11); the following clause in v. 6 indicates that this vow was treated as absolving a son from the duty of supporting his father.
notes.15:14: The Greek text here reads simply "blind guides," whereas many later manuscripts add "of the blind."
notes.15:26: Greek kynaria is a diminutive ("little dogs" or household pets), distinct from wild street dogs, contrasting the children at the table with pets in the house.
notes.15:37: Greek spyris denotes a large woven hamper or provision basket (also in 16:10), distinct from the smaller wicker basket (kophinos) mentioned in 16:9.
notes.16:3: The bracketed saying about discerning the sky (together with its opening half in v. 2 in other manuscripts) is absent from several important early witnesses, including Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.
notes.16:18: The Greek features a wordplay between Petros ("Peter," masculine) and petra ("rock," feminine, denoting a mass of rock or bedrock).
notes.16:19: The future periphrastic perfect passive verbs can be rendered either "will have been bound/loosed" (highlighting prior heavenly ratification) or "will be bound/loosed" (highlighting the resulting state).
notes.16:22: Greek hileos soi literally means "(May God be) merciful to You," an idiom of strong protest equivalent to "Far be it from You."
notes.16:25: Greek psyche here and in v. 26 encompasses both "life" and "soul"; it is rendered consistently as "life" across both verses to preserve the lexical unity.
notes.17:15: Greek seleniazetai literally means "is moonstruck," the ancient term for epilepsy or recurring seizures.
notes.17:20: Greek oligopistian means "little faith" rather than "unbelief." Verse 21 ("But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and is omitted in this critical text.
notes.17:24: Greek ta didrachma ("the two-drachma") refers to the annual half-shekel temple tax paid by adult Jewish males (Exod 30:13).
notes.17:27: A stater was a silver coin worth four drachmas, the exact sum required to pay the two-drachma temple tax for both Jesus and Peter.
notes.18:9: Greek geennan tou pyros ("Gehenna of fire") refers to the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, used as a term for the place of final punishment.
notes.18:10: Verse 11 ("For the Son of Man came to save the lost") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and is omitted in this critical text.
notes.18:15: The critical text omits "against you" (eis se), found in later manuscripts, leaving the brother's sin stated more generally.
notes.18:18: The Greek future perfect periphrastic forms (estai dedemena and estai lelymena) express that what is bound or loosed on earth "will have been bound" or "will have been loosed" in heaven.
notes.18:22: Greek hebdomēkontakis hepta literally reads "seventy times seven," though it can also be rendered "seventy-seven times" (echoing Gen 4:24 LXX); either way it signifies limitless forgiveness.
notes.19:9: Greek porneia denotes sexual immorality or marital unfaithfulness. The closing clause ("and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery") is supported by manuscripts such as Vaticanus and Ephraemi Rescriptus, while omitted in others such as Sinaiticus and Bezae.
notes.19:17: Matthew's text reads "about what is good" and "There is One who is good," whereas some later manuscripts harmonize the wording with Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19 ("Why do you call Me good?").
notes.19:21: Greek teleios means "complete," "whole," or "perfect," directly answering the young man's question about what he is still lacking (v. 20).
notes.19:28: Greek palingenesia ("rebirth" or "regeneration") refers to the future renewal of creation at the coming of the Messianic reign.
notes.19:29: Some early manuscripts omit "or wife" and read "many times as much" instead of "a hundredfold."
notes.20:2: A denarius was a Roman silver coin that served as the standard daily wage for a common laborer.
notes.20:3: Daytime hours were counted from sunrise (around 6:00 a.m.), placing the third, sixth, ninth, and eleventh hours at roughly 9:00 a.m., noon, 3:00 p.m., and 5:00 p.m.
notes.20:15: "Is your eye evil" is a Semitic idiom denoting envy or stinginess, contrasted here with the owner's "good" (generous) character.
notes.20:28: Greek lytron denotes a ransom price paid for release, and the preposition anti ("in place of" or "for") expresses substitution.
notes.21:5: Literally 'a son of a beast of burden,' a Hebraism from Zechariah 9:9 for a young donkey; the conjunction 'and' (Greek kai) may also be understood epexegetically ('even'), reflecting Hebrew poetic parallelism.
notes.21:31: The Greek text here reads 'the first,' matching the son who initially refused and later went; some ancient manuscripts reverse the order of the two sons in verses 28-30 or read 'the last' in this verse.
notes.21:41: The Greek employs an emphatic wordplay, kakous kakos apolesei (literally, 'wicked ones wickedly he will destroy'), reflected here as 'wretched ruin on those wretched men.'
notes.21:44: This verse appears in major early manuscripts (including Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and parallels Luke 20:18, though it is absent from several Western witnesses (such as Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts).
notes.22:9: The phrase 'main intersections of the roads' (Greek diexodous ton hodon) literally refers to the outlets or thoroughfares where city streets open onto country roads.
notes.22:16: 'Look at the face of people' is a literal rendering of a Semitic idiom meaning to show partiality or be swayed by someone's outward status.
notes.22:30: Some manuscripts add 'of God' after 'angels,' whereas the critical text reads simply 'like angels in heaven.'
notes.22:44: Some later manuscripts read 'a footstool for Your feet' in conformity with the Septuagint of Psalm 110:1, while the critical text reads 'beneath Your feet' (hypokato).
notes.23:8: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads καθηγητής ("instructor" or "guide") here as in 23:10, rather than διδάσκαλος ("teacher") found in other manuscripts, preserving the lexical parallel between both verses.
notes.23:13: Verse 14 (a woe regarding devouring widows' houses, parallel to Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not present in this critical text.
notes.23:15: "Gehenna" transliterates Greek γέεννα (from Hebrew Ge-Hinnom, the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem), used in the Gospels to designate the place of final judgment.
notes.23:35: The Old Testament prophet Zechariah was the son of Berechiah (Zech 1:1), whereas the Zechariah killed in the temple court in 2 Chronicles 24:20-22 was the son of Jehoiada; paired with Abel (Gen 4), the saying spans the righteous blood shed from the first to the last book of the Hebrew canon.
notes.24:3: Greek parousia means "coming" or "presence" (often used for a royal arrival), and synteleia denotes the "completion" or "close" of the age.
notes.24:28: Greek aetoi literally means "eagles," though in antiquity the term also included large carrion birds such as vultures, which fits the mention of a carcass.
notes.24:33: The clause has no explicit subject in Greek and can be translated either "He is near" (the Son of Man) or "it is near" (His coming or the end).
notes.24:36: Some later manuscripts omit "nor the Son," likely out of theological concern, whereas the earliest and best-attested witnesses include the phrase.
notes.24:51: Greek dichotomesei literally means "will cut in two," denoting either literal execution or, figuratively, severe punishment and expulsion.
notes.25:6: The Greek reads literally 'come out for a meeting' (without 'him'), using a term commonly applied to going out to welcome an arriving dignitary; 'him' is implied by context.
notes.25:13: Some later manuscripts add 'in which the Son of Man is coming,' which is absent from the earliest Greek witnesses and the Saints Greek Critical Text.
notes.25:15: A talent was a large weight of silver equal to roughly 6,000 denarii, or about twenty years of wages for a day laborer. The adverb 'Immediately' stands at the end of verse 15 in the Greek text to introduce the sentence continuing in verse 16.
notes.25:40: The phrase 'these brothers of Mine' (Greek adelphoi, which can include brothers and sisters) is variously understood as referring specifically to Christ's followers or more broadly to all people in need.
notes.26:2: Greek paradidōmi literally means "hand over" or "deliver over" and is translated consistently throughout this chapter (vv. 2, 15, 16, 21, 23-25), where it carries the sense of betrayal in Judas's actions.
notes.26:15: Greek estēsan literally means "weighed out," echoing the Septuagint wording of Zechariah 11:12 regarding the thirty pieces of silver.
notes.26:18: Greek ton deina is an indefinite expression meaning "so-and-so" or "a certain man," leaving the host unnamed.
notes.26:28: The earliest manuscripts read "My blood of the covenant" without the word "new," which was added in later manuscripts under the influence of Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25.
notes.26:45: Greek katheudete to loipon kai anapauesthe can be read either as an ironic command ("Sleep on now and take your rest") or as a question ("Are you still sleeping and resting?").
notes.26:50: Greek eph' ho parei is elliptical, literally "for which you are here," and is understood either as a command ("do what you have come for") or as a question ("why are you here?").
notes.26:64: "Power" (Greek tēs dynameōs) is a reverent Jewish circumlocution for God, combining allusions to Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13.
notes.27:6: The Greek term korbanas transliterates the Aramaic word for the sacred temple treasury, related to the term for a dedicated offering (compare Mark 7:11).
notes.27:9: Although Matthew names Jeremiah, the wording draws primarily on Zechariah 11:12-13 blended with potter and field imagery from Jeremiah (Jeremiah 18:1-12; 19:1-13; 32:6-15), attributing the composite quotation to the major prophet.
notes.27:17: Some manuscripts read "Jesus Barabbas" here and in verse 16, heightening the contrast with "Jesus who is called Christ," but the earliest and broadest witnesses read simply "Barabbas."
notes.27:24: Greek "of this blood" can also be construed as "of this man's blood"; many later manuscripts add "righteous" ("of the blood of this righteous man"), echoing verse 19.
notes.27:46: The Greek text here reads the Aramaic form "Eloi, Eloi" (as in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus), whereas other manuscripts read the Hebrew form "Eli, Eli," which more directly explains the bystanders' confusion with "Elijah" in verse 47.
notes.27:49: Several early Alexandrian manuscripts insert a sentence here stating that another took a spear and pierced His side, and water and blood came out (compare John 19:34), which is absent from our Greek text and most witnesses.
notes.27:54: Because "Son of God" lacks the definite article in Greek, the phrase can be translated either "the Son of God" or "a son of God"; within Matthew's narrative it directly answers the taunts in verses 40 and 43.
notes.27:65: The Greek verb echete is ambiguous in form and can be read either as an indicative ("You have a guard") or as an imperative ("Take a guard").
notes.28:1: The Greek phrase opse sabbaton can mean "late on the Sabbath," but in Hellenistic Greek opse with the genitive regularly means "after," matching the following clause describing the dawn of the first day of the week.
notes.28:6: Later Greek manuscripts add "the Lord" ("where the Lord was lying"), whereas the earliest witnesses omit the title and read simply "where He was lying."
notes.28:17: The Greek verb distazo ("doubted" or "hesitated") and the construction hoi de ("yet some") are debated as to whether a portion of the eleven wavered or whether the disciples as a whole felt initial hesitation alongside worship.
notes.28:19: The Greek preposition eis ("into the name") conveys entry into allegiance and relationship with the singular "name" of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
